title: S121 later notes: render pane robustness and wording

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Later notes from the S121 relay (run-20261026-132255-77bf, landed b76abc0), not fixed in that slice:
- Out-of-order run.render answers for the same render can show a stale one; use a per-pane sequence number.
- A corrupt run.json is reported as "no run".
- renderOn() resets pane state from the draw path.
- Help's pgup/pgdown wording does not mention renders; "?" does nothing while the run pane is open (predates S121).
- Side-scroll for renders wider than the pane.
- A read error in uiRenders reads as "wrote none"; the card should say why renders could not be read.
- The 24 KiB byte cut can leave an escape-sequence fragment (cosmetic).
- The render size shown is informational; the file is re-read at fetch.
- No socket-level test against a real daemon, and no real vendor UI pass writing the files has been tested.
- Merge with S106 (outer session, 2026-10-26): the pane takes the whole body while a render shows and is inline under its row otherwise (internal/tui/view.go screen()); check that this reads right live.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestOutOfOrderRenderAnswerKeepsTheLatest` (`internal/tui/renders_test.go`): ask for render 1 (call 1), press `v` through the others and back to render 1 (call 4); answer call 4 with `SECOND`, then call 1 with `FIRST`; the view shows `SECOND`.
- `TestRenderAnswerFromAClosedPaneIsIgnored` (`internal/tui/renders_test.go`): ask, close the pane, reopen it, deliver the old answer: the view shows `Loading`.
- `TestRunRenderSaysWhenTheRecordIsUnreadable` (`internal/daemon/render_test.go`): a run whose `run.json` is not valid JSON gives a non-`not_found` error naming the run and saying it cannot be read; an unknown run and `../r1` stay `not_found`; the same for `run.report`.
- `TestCardSaysWhyRendersCouldNotBeRead` (`internal/engine/renders_test.go`): a renders directory with mode 0 sets `card.RendersError`; a missing directory leaves it empty; the TUI shows `Renders: the UI pass (round 1) could not be read: <why>` instead of `wrote none`.
- `TestRenderOnDoesNotWritePaneState` (`internal/tui/renders_test.go`): swap the card so the render is gone; `*h.m.pane` is unchanged across `h.view()` and `renderOn()`; `v` and `esc` still return to the card.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
UI slice: UI pass (r14). Tests first. Line anchors are from main at 7d5bfb8 (2026-10-30); re-anchor.
1. Sequence. Add a model-wide `renderSeq int` that never restarts; add `seq` to `renderFetch` and `renderMsg` (`internal/tui/card.go` about :172-179); bump it in `fetchRender` (about :209-230) and store it with the pending fetch; `renderArrived` (about :232-243) ignores an answer unless a fetch exists for the key with the same `seq`.
2. Unreadable record. Add `ErrBadRunID` to `validID` (`internal/runrec/store.go` about :55-60). Add a daemon helper `openRun(id)`: `not_found` "no run X" for `ErrBadRunID` or `os.ErrNotExist`, otherwise a plain error "run X cannot be read: ..." (code `internal`, no new wire code). Use it in `runRender` and `runReport` (`internal/daemon/runs.go`); leave `loadFinishedEngine` for later. Update `docs/design.md` (run.render).
3. Renders error. Add `RendersError string` (`json:"renders_error,omitempty"`) to `ApprovalCard` (`internal/runrec/record.go`, beside `checks_error`). `listRenders` (`internal/engine/approval.go` about :209-225) returns an error when the directory exists but cannot be read; `uiRenders` sets the field from it or from a listed file that cannot be read; `rendersLine` (`card.go` about :128-141) shows the reason before the `wrote none` case. Update `docs/state.md` and `docs/dashboard.md`.
4. Draw path. Make `renderOn` (`card.go` about :153-163) pure: it returns 0 for a gone render without writing `m.pane.render`; `nextRender` and `esc` already reset the field.
5. `go test ./internal/tui -update` if a golden changes; review the diff.

Owner decisions 2026-10-30 (interactive, spec drafting): the render sequence counter lives on the model and never restarts, stored per fetch; an unreadable run.json gives code internal with the message run X cannot be read (no new wire code); the read error travels in a new renders_error card field like checks_error; this slice fixes renders only, and the same draw-path and ordering issues in the S176 report viewer (reportOn, fetchReport) go to a follow-up. The polish notes (help pgup/pgdown wording, side-scroll, the 24 KiB escape fragment, size, real-daemon tests) stay later.
